{{nihongo|'''Ōarahiko Shrine'''|大荒比古神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Yasuigawa, Shin-Asahi-chō, {{ill|Takashima, Shiga|Q845794|qid=Q845794}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358}}. Until early {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}, it was called '''Kawachi Daimyōjin'''. It is a {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}} for a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}. The {{ill|Reisai|fr|Festival Reisai|ja|例祭|simple|Reisai|qid=Q11385469}} is the '''Nanakawa Festival'''. Its former shrine rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. {{nihongo|'''Ōarahiko Shrine'''|大荒比古神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōaratawake-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Prince Toyokiirihiko|Q11633375|qid=Q11633375}}
These two are the main deities; additionally enshrined are {{ill|Sukunabikona|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|qid=Q3275687}}, {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|qid=Q313119}}, {{ill|Emperor Uda|Q349267|qid=Q349267}}, and {{ill|Atsumi-shinnō|Q11499521|qid=Q11499521}}. The main deities are said to grant victory.

== Rituals ==
== Sacred events ==
* Nanakawa Festival
:Held on May 4. Includes "yakko-furi" and {{ill|Yabusame|Q1886157|qid=Q1886157}}, and is said to be the leading festival in the Kosei area of Shiga. "Yakko-furi" (target procession, barrel-swinging) is selected as a Shiga Prefecture intangible folk cultural property. The barrel-swinging “witticisms” are bawdy and entertain spectators.
* Kentō Festival
:A summer festival organized by the Ōarahiko Shrine parish youth association, held in mid-August.

== Shrine families ==
:According to the Kitano Tenmangū document ''Meian-tō Shoki Roku Kakinuki'' (record of December 4, {{ill|Bun'an|Q1193586|qid=Q1193586}} 4), the shrine family at that time was involved in conflict between {{ill|Enryaku-ji|Q917195|qid=Q917195}} and the {{ill|Takashima clan|Q11669657|qid=Q11669657}}, and was exiled to {{ill|Kyushu|Q13987|qid=Q13987}}. Thereafter, worship has continued through the current shrine family.
